doc-org-invite.title: 1. Create Organization & Invite Members
doc-org-invite.summary: Guide to creating an organization, assigning roles (Owner, DevOps, Viewer), and sending email invitations.
steps: Step 1: Go to "My Organizations" in the Personal Portal or open the Organization Dashboard.
Step 2: Click "+ Create Organization", enter the company name and URL slug identifier.
Step 3: Under "Members & Permissions", click "+ Invite Member", enter the work email, and assign a role (SME_OWNER, DEVOPS, or VIEWER).
Step 4: The invited member receives an email notification and can click "Accept" directly in the Notification Center.
doc-org-invite.tips: Note: Only SME_OWNER or Administrator accounts have permission to invite members or revoke member access.

doc-agent-k8s.title: 2. Register Agent & Connect Kubernetes Cluster
doc-agent-k8s.summary: How to deploy the selfheal-agent Helm chart on K8s clusters (AWS EKS, GKE, or On-Premise bare-metal).
steps: Step 1: Navigate to "K8s Clusters" (/dashboard/clusters) -> click "Register New Cluster".
Step 2: Name your cluster (e.g., `k8s-prod-hn-01`) and select the infrastructure provider.
Step 3: Copy the auto-generated Helm install command containing your secret Agent Token.
Step 4: Run `helm install selfheal-agent ./charts/selfheal-agent --set clusterId=...` from your admin workstation.
doc-agent-k8s.tips: Requires Linux kernel >= 5.8 with BPF CO-RE (Compile Once - Run Everywhere) enabled.

doc-agent-health.title: 3. Verify Agent Connection Health
doc-agent-health.summary: Verify eBPF Telemetry Probe status, WebSocket heartbeat, and real-time telemetry streaming.
steps: Step 1: Open the K8s Clusters list or Agent Management page (/dashboard/agents).
Step 2: Locate your Agent name and verify the green "100% ONLINE" status badge.
Step 3: Check the latest Heartbeat latency (must be under 5 seconds).
Step 4: If the status shows "DEGRADED" or "DISCONNECTED", inspect egress firewall rules for ports 443 and 5000.
doc-agent-health.tips: You can run `kubectl logs -n selfheal-system daemonset/selfheal-agent` to inspect live startup logs.

doc-metrics-ai.title: 4. View Metrics, Logs, Events & AI Predictions
doc-metrics-ai.summary: Leverage the time-series AI engine to detect CPU saturation, memory leaks, and Pod conflicts early.
steps: Step 1: Open "Resource Metrics" (/dashboard/monitoring/metrics) to view CPU, RAM, and Network I/O charts.
Step 2: Open "AI Risk Forecast" (/dashboard/ai/predictions) to inspect early saturation risk warnings.
Step 3: Review growth slope rate and estimated time remaining before an OOM (Out Of Memory) event.
doc-metrics-ai.tips: The AI model forecasts incident risks 15 to 45 minutes in advance, giving engineers ample time to prepare mitigation.

doc-rca.title: 5. Inspect Root Cause Analysis (RCA)
doc-rca.summary: Use causal graph AI to pinpoint the exact Pod or service triggering cascading failures.
steps: Step 1: When an incident triggers, go to "Incident Management" -> select the "Root Cause Analysis (RCA)" tab.
Step 2: Inspect the Dependency Call Graph and Confidence Score (e.g., 94.2%).
Step 3: Review recommended actions such as "Increase memory limit from 512Mi to 1Gi" or "Restart Pod payment-gw-7b9".
doc-rca.tips: RCA automatically correlates Kubernetes Events (Evicted, Unhealthy, BackOff) with telemetry signals.

doc-self-healing.title: 6. Configure & Track Self-Healing
doc-self-healing.summary: Configure automated remediation policies and Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) emergency approvals.
steps: Step 1: On "Automation Policies" (/dashboard/self-healing/policies), enable rules such as Restart Pod or Scale Up Replica.
Step 2: For high-risk actions (Drain Node, Rollback Deployment), the system creates an approval request in "Approval Gate (HITL)".
Step 3: An SME Owner or DevOps Lead reviews the rationale and clicks "Approve Action".
Step 4: Track execution outcomes in "Healing History" to confirm the workload returns to Healthy status.
doc-self-healing.tips: The Safe Remediation Rate-Limiter automatically pauses an action if it fails 3 consecutive times.

doc-rbac-security.title: 7. Configure Roles & Security Policies
doc-rbac-security.summary: Least Privilege separation across Super Admin, Admin, SME Owner, DevOps, and Viewer roles.
steps: Step 1: Super Administrators configure the role matrix in the System Admin Console (/admin/roles).
Step 2: Maintain strict separation between Platform-level permissions and Tenant-level permissions.
Step 3: Audit all role assignments via "SHA-256 Audit Logs" (/admin/audit-logs).
doc-rbac-security.tips: Do not grant SUPER_ADMIN privileges to engineers who only manage a single organization.

faq-1.question: Why can't the Agent connect to the Backend?
faq-1.answer: The most common cause is a firewall blocking the WebSocket endpoint (/api/v1/telemetry/ws) or an expired Agent Token. Verify outbound HTTPS/WSS connectivity from the K8s cluster to the Backend domain and regenerate a fresh Token on the Agent Management page.

faq-2.question: Why is my Cluster not showing Metrics?
faq-2.answer: The platform requires the selfheal-agent DaemonSet to run on at least 1 worker node with kubelet cAdvisor healthy. If using OpenShift or Bottlerocket, please verify SELinux policies for the eBPF socket.

faq-3.question: Why did AI predict an anomaly without triggering self-healing?
faq-3.answer: Automated remediation only runs when the matching policy is set to "AUTOMATIC" and the AI confidence score exceeds the threshold (default > 85%). If the policy is set to "HITL_REQUIRED", the action waits for manual approval.

faq-4.question: Why was a Restart Pod action rejected?
faq-4.answer: The platform enforces a Circuit Breaker: if healthy Pods in a Deployment would fall below the PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) or the Pod has restarted more than 5 times in the past hour, automated restarts are blocked to prevent full service outage.

faq-5.question: How do I invite members to my Organization?
faq-5.answer: Open the Organization Dashboard -> "Organization" -> "Members & Permissions" -> click "+ Invite Member". Enter their email and select the desired role. The invitee will see the invitation in their Personal Portal.

faq-6.question: How do I revoke a member's access?
faq-6.answer: In the organization member list, locate the user, open the three-dot menu -> select "Remove from Organization" or "Change Role" to Viewer. Infrastructure and resource access is revoked immediately.
